Under the initiative, the Federal Government has already reached more than 500,000 farmers through the Bank of Agriculture (BOA), while the President has approved a N1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the bank to expand access to affordable financing across the agricultural value chain.
Tinubu Unveils Plans To Modernise Irrigation, Engages Youths In Agriculture
The interventions are also expected to increase the number of beneficiaries to two million farmers and support the cultivation of 500,000 hectares of farmland under the Renewed Hope Agenda.
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council disclosed this in a statement issued on Sunday by its spokesperson, Dele Alake.
According to the statement, the administration’s agricultural interventions go beyond providing loans to farmers to include access to quality seeds, fertiliser, mechanisation, irrigation, storage facilities and commodity markets.
It said the Renewed Hope Smallholder Support and Value Chain Fund, with a programme value of N250 billion, was financing farmers through Farmer Aggregation Companies responsible for coordinating registration, input distribution, extension services and market linkages.
The programme, according to the council, has reached more than 500,000 smallholder farmers across 16 states, including over 70,000 women.
It has also facilitated the distribution of approximately 2.5 million bags of fertiliser and 300,000 bags of certified seeds.
The initiative is targeting two million farmers and plans to distribute more than 10 million bags of fertiliser.
States benefiting from the programme include Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Niger, Borno, Gombe, Taraba, Adamawa, Yobe and Bauchi, among others.
To protect farmers from market uncertainties and distress sales, the Bank of Agriculture is also implementing a N200 billion Guaranteed Minimum Price Programme.
Under the scheme, the bank has procured approximately 170,000 metric tonnes of maize, rice, sorghum and cassava to strengthen commodity markets and provide farmers with more reliable outlets for their produce.
The council also highlighted the bank’s Onion Financing Programme, developed in partnership with the National Onion Producers, Processors and Marketers Association of Nigeria (NOPPMAN), which represents more than 11,800 onion farmers.
The initiative is designed to provide farmers with improved seeds and fertiliser, while supporting processors with commodity purchase funds and the development of storage and solar-powered cooling facilities to reduce post-harvest losses.
Under the financing arrangement, cooperatives will contribute 30 per cent of their input costs, while the Bank of Agriculture will provide the remaining 70 per cent.
On the approved N1.5 trillion recapitalisation of the Bank of Agriculture, the council said the move would strengthen the institution’s capacity to provide accessible funding to farmers, agricultural cooperatives, processors, aggregators and other businesses across the agricultural value chain.
It said the recapitalisation was also expected to position the bank to support large-scale agricultural investments, expand its operations into underserved farming communities and mobilise additional resources for domestic food production.
The council noted that the recapitalisation was among Tinubu’s major campaign promises in 2023.
Other interventions highlighted include dry-season farming financing, agricultural mechanisation, ginger recovery, women’s cooperative financing, youth participation and commercial poultry production.
Under the dry-season farming programme, the bank is working with the All-Farmers Association of Nigeria to develop a pipeline targeting 400,000 farmers for the 2026 farming cycle.
The programme includes financing for 120,000 hectares of wheat cultivation and another 300,000 hectares for rice, maize, sorghum, millet, cassava and soybeans.
Similarly, the Nigeria Ginger Recovery Programme has supported 3,200 farmers in Kachia, Kaduna State, with blight-free seeds.
The initiative has also recovered more than 9,000 bags of ginger for multiplication, with plans to expand cultivation across 20,000 hectares in 16 states.
The bank is also targeting at least 50,000 women nationwide through insured cooperative production financing at nine per cent, in partnership with the Federal Ministries of Women Affairs and Agriculture.
In the area of mechanisation, the Renewed Hope National Agricultural Mechanisation Programme has deployed 1,571 tractors to 23 states.
The tractors are expected to support the mechanisation of 1.2 million hectares of farmland, with farming communities accessing the equipment through qualified Mechanisation Service Providers.
Additionally, the council said the administration was implementing a ₦385 billion productive-use-of-electricity programme involving the provision of 44,000 electric cargo tricycles and 100,000 solar irrigation pumps.
The campaign council said the various interventions demonstrated the administration’s commitment to making agriculture a major driver of economic growth, food security and job creation.
